_note: A worked example of one day-one sitting, shown on the opening screen so the finished artifact is visible with no key and no ten-minute exercise. The person is invented; the explorer's record is real and the page says which is which. Swap this file to change the example; nothing here is hardcoded in index.html.

answers.question: What is taking up most of your mind right now?
answers.answer: My mother goes into assisted living in February and I am the one who has to tell her. My brother says he will come for the move but not for the conversation.
answers.followup: You said your brother will come for the move but not the conversation. Who decided that — him, or the two of you?
answers.followupAnswer: Nobody decided it. It settled that way about fifteen years ago and we have both been calling it logistics ever since.
answers.why: The division of that work is doing quiet damage; worth asking who chose it.

answers.question: What are you pretending to be fine about?
answers.answer: The miscarriage in March. I tell people we are fine, and we are mostly fine, and I would like to stop being asked about it.
answers.why: She has just asked not to be asked. A follow-up here would be extraction, not interest.

answers.question: What do you want Noor to know about who you are at 38?
answers.answer: That I was frightened of nearly everything and did it anyway, and that those are not opposites. Her grandmother believed they were and it cost her most of her twenties.
answers.why: Specific and finished. A follow-up would only pad it.

answers.question: What are you still deciding?
answers.answer: Whether to leave the hospital and go back to teaching. Everyone seems to think I have already decided. I have not.
answers.followup: You said everyone thinks you have decided. What did they see that made them think so?
answers.followupAnswer: I applied for one job and mentioned it to three people. I think I wanted to watch their faces when I said it.
answers.why: The gap between what she has let people see and what is true is the real question.

naming.title: Frightened and moving anyway
naming.why: Two of the four answers turn on the same gap — what she has let people see against what is actually true. The name is her own phrasing: she used "frightened" and "did it anyway" in one sentence and said they are not opposites.
naming.lede: At thirty-eight she was carrying two decisions by herself and had let almost no one see either one.
